1.caption: Figure 1. ARBITER assessment workflow. The language-model agent finds evidence and answers questions. Software binds selected text to captured documents, applies RoB 2 algorithms and exports the assessment record. Binding locates text; it does not establish support for an answer. The audit file contains source identifiers and selected evidence, not complete documents. Reviewer approval is part of the general workflow but was not tested in the benchmark. AI indicates artificial intelligence; MCP, Model Context Protocol; RoB 2, the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool.
1.alt: A language-model agent searches captured trial documents, records answers and selects evidence. Software binds selected text to the captured extraction, applies RoB 2 algorithms and exports an assessment record. Reviewer approval belongs to the general workflow and was not tested in the benchmark. The audit file contains source identifiers and selected evidence, not complete source files. Binding locates text and does not establish that it supports an answer.
1.title: ARBITER assessment workflow

2.caption: Figure 2. AVATAR assessment linking evidence, answers and ratings. AVATAR compares early surgery with watchful waiting for asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis; the outcome is all-cause death. The example illustrates the workflow, not typical performance. Its rationales were not independently validated. Letter/page tabs identify sources; counterevidence and unknowns remain visible. A No information answer about the dated analysis plan contributes to Some concerns overall. Footer labels concern D5, not independently rated Overall judgments. The simplified Overall rule omits permitted escalation to High when multiple Some concerns domains substantially lower confidence. The displayed P value does not establish adequate randomization. Y indicates yes; PY, probably yes; PN, probably no; N, no; NI, no information; D5, selection of the reported result; AI, artificial intelligence; RoB 2, the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool.
2.alt: AVATAR's five domains link source excerpts, model answers, software checks and ratings. Four domains are Low. A No information answer about the dated analysis plan contributes to Some concerns for selection of the reported result and Overall. Counterevidence and unknowns remain visible. The figure illustrates a model assessment; its rationales were not independently validated. The simplified Overall rule does not show every permitted escalation.
2.title: AVATAR assessment linking evidence, answers and ratings

3.caption: Figure 3. Paired evaluation and blinded label choices. Both model arms used the same reported model identifier and documents for 102 trials. Human reviews covered all 510 domain cells before reviewers saw labels. Choices were among three anonymized labels in random order without rationales. The conditional comparison uses 60 agreed choices from 80 cells where arms differed; 20 split choices enter sensitivities. Agreement analyses use all 510 cells.
3.alt: Three parallel assessment lanes for ARBITER, Direct prompting and two independent human reviews across 102 trials and 510 domain cells. A separate conditional branch contains 80 arm-discordant cells, 60 agreed choices and 20 splits.
3.title: Paired evaluation and blinded label choices

4.caption: Figure 4. Domain agreement with human reviews and published labels. Blue circles show ARBITER; orange squares, Direct prompting. Bars show 95% CIs. Diamonds show paired ARBITER minus Direct prompting differences in percentage points; zero lines indicate no difference. Each human review includes 510 pooled cells, 102 per domain. Human agreement provides context, not a performance ceiling. D1, randomisation process; D2, deviations from intended interventions; D3, missing outcome data; D4, outcome measurement; D5, selection of the reported result. CI, confidence interval. Intervals use 10,000 percentile bootstrap resamples of trials within reviews.
4.alt: Exact agreement and paired gains against each human reviewer, pooled and by domain. Both pooled gains favor ARBITER; D5 gains are largest and D3 depends strongly on the human reviewer reference. The full-cohort Published comparison is shown separately.
4.title: Domain agreement with human reviews and published labels

5.caption: Figure 5. Paired differences in signaling-answer agreement. Diamonds and bars show paired ARBITER minus Direct prompting differences and 95% CIs. The sample size is the number of answer components evaluable in both arms. Five-level coding keeps yes, probably yes, no, probably no and no information separate. Collapsed coding merges definite and probable answers, retaining no information. Eligibility and question-level results are in eTables 11 to 13. D1, randomisation process; D2, deviations from intended interventions; D3, missing outcome data; D4, outcome measurement; D5, selection of the reported result. CI, confidence interval. Intervals use 10,000 percentile bootstrap resamples of trials within reviews.
5.alt: Paired signaling-answer differences by domain and human reviewer, separating five-level and collapsed coding. D3 changes direction with coding against Human Review 1; D5 collapsed gains are smaller against Human Review 2.
5.title: Paired differences in signaling-answer agreement
